PIEROLOOS — package-lock.json generation package

GitHub currently has no package-lock.json. Because the project's manifest uses
"latest" for several packages, an authoritative lockfile must be generated by
npm itself from the exact package.json that will be committed. Do not use a
hand-edited lockfile with invented integrity/transitive metadata.

1. Put the corrected package.json beside this file.
2. In that project directory run:

   npm install --package-lock-only --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund

3. The generated package-lock.json is the authoritative lockfile.
4. Commit package.json and package-lock.json together.
5. Then CI can safely use:

   npm ci

6. Re-enable setup-node npm caching only after package-lock.json is committed.

Recommended final CI install step:

   - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
     with:
       node-version: 22
       cache: npm

   - run: npm ci --no-audit --no-fund

The included template is only a reference and MUST NOT be renamed to
package-lock.json and treated as a finished lockfile.
